questions.question: What is the critical rendering path in a browser? Walk through each step.
questions.title: Critical Rendering Path Explained — HTML → CSSOM → Render Tree → Paint
questions.direct_answer:
What is the critical rendering path in a browser? Walk through each step.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** HTML → DOM, CSS → CSSOM, Render Tree, Layout, Paint, Composite; render-blocking resources; async/defer/preload.

**Classic weak answer:** Confusing Layout with Paint — Layout (reflow) computes positions; Paint fills pixels; Composite assembles GPU layers.

**Senior finish:** Show how <script> blocks parsing; compare async/defer/module; mention Speculation Rules API for prefetch/prerender.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Critical Rendering Path Explained — HTML → CSSOM → Render Tree → Paint** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is the critical rendering path in a browser? Walk through each step.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **HTML → DOM, CSS → CSSOM, Render Tree, Layout, Paint, Composite; render-blocking resources; async/defer/preload**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Confusing Layout with Paint — Layout (reflow) computes positions; Paint fills pixels; Composite assembles GPU layers**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Show how <script> blocks parsing; compare async/defer/module; mention Speculation Rules API for prefetch/prerender**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** HTML → DOM, CSS → CSSOM, Render Tree, Layout, Paint, Composite; render-blocking resources; async/defer/preload
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Mental model (flowchart)
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TB
    NET[HTML + CSS + JS download] --> PARSE[Parse DOM + CSSOM]
    PARSE --> TREE[Render tree + layout]
    TREE --> PAINT[Paint + composite layers]
    PAINT --> LCP[LCP element timing]
    subgraph Perf["Performance hooks"]
        PRE[preload / prefetch]
        LAZY[lazy images + code-split]
    end
    NET --> PRE
    TREE --> LAZY
```

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **confusing Layout with Paint — Layout (reflow) computes positions; Paint fills pixels; Composite assembles GPU layers** and what you do instead.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **HTML → DOM, CSS → CSSOM, Render Tree, Layout, Paint, Composite; render-blocking resources; async/defer/preload** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Confusing Layout with Paint — Layout (reflow) computes positions; Paint fills pixels; Composite assembles GPU layers** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

questions.question: What is the difference between reflow, repaint, and composite in a browser?
questions.title: Reflow vs Repaint vs Composite — Browser Rendering Stages
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between reflow, repaint, and composite in a browser?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Reflow (Layout): geometry changes; Repaint: pixel changes without geometry; Composite: GPU layers merge; cost order: reflow > repaint > composite.

**Classic weak answer:** Animating width/height/top/left — triggers reflow; prefer transform/opacity which only composite.

**Senior finish:** Name the 'compositor-only' properties (transform, opacity, filter); will-change hint and its costs.
